{"notes":"Analysis from the PKIX-cr8 pass (2026-11-25). Recommend closing as speculative rather than implementing.

The bead asserts that 'consumers will reinvent batch fetch/check wrappers'. That is a prediction, and no consumer has asked. A batch API's shape is almost entirely determined by questions only a consumer can answer: whether fetches run concurrently and with what parallelism, whether results come back in request order, what happens on partial failure (fail the batch, return per-item results, or return the first determinative verdict), and whether one shared deadline or per-item timeouts apply. Guessing those commits public API that is hard to change later.

The 'callbacks are the right shape' half of this bead is the same conclusion PKIX-cr8.9 reached about telemetry; the two should be designed together, once there is a consumer, rather than separately now.

Note also that the pieces for a consumer-side batch already exist and are public: extract_cdp_http_urls / extract_aia_http_urls do no I/O, and CrlChecker / OcspChecker take owned bytes, so a consumer can fetch many URLs concurrently with their own client and verify the results however they like. async_fetcher's module docs now document that split (added for PKIX-cr8.1), which is the most useful thing this epic can offer without a consumer driving the design."}
